official_sources: GOV.UK Party Wall etc Act explanatory booklet
official_measurement_examples: Party Wall Act is a civil framework separate from planning permission and building-regulations approval
covered work includes party-wall work boundary construction and specified nearby excavation
notice periods depend on the relevant type of work
failure to agree can trigger surveyor/award procedure
an award controls how and when works proceed but is not planning permission
county-court appeal period for an award is 14 days under current GOV.UK guidance
the Act does not determine every legal boundary issue
party-wall compliance does not establish ownership access or final development yield
core_rules: party wall award is not planning permission
planning permission is not party wall consent
neighbour agreement is not ownership transfer
party wall is not every boundary feature
3m and 6m excavation tests are context specific
award does not create development rights
award does not establish exact title boundary
civil dispute route is distinct from planning enforcement
party wall rights do not prove access rights
party wall rights do not prove utility capacity
party wall status does not calculate yield
court appeal period must retain date context
no parcel party-wall clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, MHCLG and Party Wall etc Act sources checked 2026-07-26. Civil-law/planning/building-control and notice/award distinctions retained; no parcel promotion.
